correctness.rationale: The unit path has the simple cosine spectrum λ_k=2−2 cos(πk/n) with normalized half-step eigenvector entries. If d=gcd(2j−1,n)>1, the mode k=n/d has a cosine zero. Otherwise multiplication by 2j−1 permutes the residue pairs ±k modulo 2n, preserving the product of squared cosines; the fixed classes 0 and n are excluded from the permutation. The sine product gives ∏_{k=1}^{n−1}cos²(πk/(2n))=n/4^(n−1), so including eigenvector normalization gives ∏_k v_k(j)²=(2n)^(1−n). The Vandermonde then fixes the nonzero absolute Kalman determinant independent of j; the distance-triangular endpoint basis gives value one. In modal coordinates W_j has the common time kernel flanked by the diagonal input vector; distinct exponentials on a positive interval make the kernel positive definite, including μ=0 with the time-integral convention at the constant mode. This proves the two determinant cases and φ(2n) maximizing sites; for powers of two this is every site. The positive-damping infinite-horizon Cauchy identity and the small-time trace difference are also consistent. The common value is for each fixed (T,μ), not numerically constant as those parameters change. Independently generating the actual edge Krylov matrices and eliminating modulo 1009 at all sites of orders 21,22,25,27,30,32 gave respectively 12,20,20,18,16,32 nonzero residues, all ±1 and at precisely the predicted sites. This is corroboration, not the proof; the supplied code was read without execution.

evidence: At unit weights the cut polynomials are the grounded arm polynomials P_a,P_b for a=j−1,b=n−j. P_a is the monic odd-angle factor of U_{2a}(1−z/2): by the Chebyshev recurrence it is (−1)^a[U_a(1−z/2)−U_{a−1}(1−z/2)] for a>0, and U_{2a}=U_a²−U_{a−1}². Louboutin's |Res(U_{2a},U_{2b})|=2^{4ab} in the coprime-label case becomes modulus one for the monic affine transforms. Multiplicativity forces each integer factor resultant, in particular |Res(P_a,P_b)|, to be one. A common odd g>1 gives the shared odd angle π/g and zero. Empty blocks have resultant one. The label gcd is gcd(2j−1,2n−2j+1)=gcd(2j−1,n). Thus the stronger theorem gives the exact zero-or-unit determinant and common nonzero det H_T/Δ² under all the stated horizons and damping, and at infinite time for μ>0. The endpoint eigenvector sine product gives Δ⁻²=(2n)^(1−n); the totient count is immediate.
